messages:
maya: Throwing an idea onto the table: explicit residency header + short region lease to reduce legal-risk writes. Header example: X-Redwood-Residency: eu_only or X-Redwood-Residency: global. Also return a consent stamp so clients can prove where a write was accepted.

arun: Intent is good. Main worry is split-brain and conflicting commits if two regions think they own a tenant. Need a clear takeover safety protocol.

sofie: Operational pattern that could work: local sync commit for 'eu_only' tenants, then async replication via escrow queue to other regions. Escrow items are quarantined until acknowledged. ops-bot: created ticket R-4591 for escrow operator runbook.

ben: Practical add: short leases per tenant (ttl ~ 30s). Only lease holder accepts primary writes. Other regions can accept writes if they have a takeover token or verify lease expiry. This avoids heavyweight global locks.

maya: Minimal proxy sketch: 
```
Client -> Edge (adds X-Redwood-Residency: eu_only)
Edge -> Local proxy checks residency cache
if lease.exists(tenant) and lease.owner == local_region: serve locally
else if local_model_variant.available: serve locally (quantized) and mark replicate_async
else: forward to primary region with X-Redwood-Residency-Fallback: remote
```
Also include X-Redwood-Consent-Stamp: sha256(tenant+lease+timestamp) in responses.

laura: Metric suggestions: residency.local_hit, residency.remote_forward, residency.takeover_requests, escrow.queue_depth. Audit: log consent-stamp and hashed tenant id for compliance.

arun: Rollout idea: canary 5% EU tenants; monitor conflicting-writes/sec and escrow backlog. Auto-rollback if divergence crosses threshold.

sofie: Short operator runbook (high level):
- check lease: 'rwctl leases show tenant:<id>'
- prewarm model variant: 'opsctl model prewarm --model gptq-local --tenant <id>'
- pause remote forward: 'routerctl set-route <tenant> freeze-remote-forward true'
- inspect escrow: 'escrowctl peek tenant:<id>'
Add an emergency manual takeover path that quarantines escrow by default.

ben: Two other points: 1) quantized local variants change output distribution -> require eval gates and rollback hooks, 2) per-tenant prewarm costs could be high; prefer warm-cache heuristics and reuse across tenants.

maya: Agree. Optimize should compute a variant-compatibility score and recommended fallback policy per tenant. Default: remote primary unless tenant opts into local-only after legal signoff.

laura: For audit retention, add a retention flag on tenant profiles so compliance customers can extend consent-stamp/audit logs retention.

arun: Takeover safety refinement: require a three-way handshake for takeover: request -> origin-region heartbeat-check -> commit. If origin unresponsive for > lease-ttl * 2, allow operator-assisted commit. This reduces accidental split-brain.

sofie: Also add a takeover-precheck that fails if escrow queue depth > threshold. That prevents losing writes during contested takeover.

maya: Action items: 1) write RFC spec for headers and lease semantics, 2) prototype edge-proxy behavior (honor header, emit consent-stamp), 3) dashboard with metrics above. I'll open RFC PR and link escrow runbook.

deploy-bot: staged rollout created: residency-lease-gating v0.1 -> canary 5% (ticket R-4591).

ben: :thumbsup: keep the eval and Canary SLOs strict.

laura: I'll update enterprise onboarding checklist to include the audit retention option.

maya: Thanks team — will post RFC when ready.
